sanskrit: na cānuśiṣyed rājānam apṛcchantaṃ kadā cana tūṣṇīṃ tv enam upāsīta kāle samabhipūjayan
english: One should never instruct a king who has not asked; rather, one should wait upon him in silence, showing reverence at the proper time.

sanskrit: asūyanti hi rājāno janān anṛtavādinaḥ tathaiva cāvamanyante mantriṇaṃ vādinaḥ mṛṣā
english: For kings take offense at those who speak falsely, and they likewise hold in contempt a minister who utters falsehoods.

sanskrit: naiṣāṃ dāreṣu kurvīta maitrīṃ prājñaḥ kathaṃ cana antaḥpuracarā ye ca dveṣṭi yānahitāś ca ye
english: A wise man should never in any way cultivate friendship with the wives of kings, nor with those who dwell in the inner apartments, nor with those who are hostile or unfavorable to him.

sanskrit: vidite cāsya kurvīta kāryāṇi sulaghūny api evaṃ vicarato rājño na kṣatir jāyate kva cit
english: One should perform even the smallest duties with the king's knowledge; a king whose servant acts thus suffers no harm anywhere.

sanskrit: yatnāc copacared enam agnivad devavac ca ha anṛtenopacīrṇo hi hiṃsyād enam asaṃśayam
english: One should serve him with care, as one would serve fire or a god; for one who serves him with deceit will undoubtedly harm him.

sanskrit: yac ca bhartānuyuñjīta tad evābhyanuvartayet pramādam avahelāṃ ca kopaṃ ca parivarjayet
english: Whatever the master enjoins, one should carry out accordingly; one should shun negligence, contempt, and anger.

sanskrit: samarthanāsu sarvāsu hitaṃ ca priyam eva ca saṃvarṇayet tad evāsya priyād api hitaṃ vadet
english: In all matters where one is capable, one should represent what is both beneficial and pleasing; indeed, one should speak what is beneficial to him even above what is merely pleasing.

sanskrit: anukūlo bhavec cāsya sarvārtheṣu kathāsu ca apriyaṃ cāhitaṃ yat syāt tad asmai nānuvarṇayet
english: One should be agreeable to him in all matters and conversations, and should not describe to him anything that is displeasing or harmful.

sanskrit: nāham asya priyo 'smīti matvā seveta paṇḍitaḥ apramattaś ca yattaś ca hitaṃ kuryāt priyaṃ ca yat
english: A wise man should not serve with the thought 'I am not dear to him'; rather, being vigilant and attentive, he should do what is beneficial and pleasing.

sanskrit: nāsyāniṣṭāni seveta nāhitaiḥ saha saṃvaset svasthānān na vikampeta sa rājavasatiṃ vaset
english: One should not pursue what is undesired by him, should not dwell with those who are hostile to him, should not waver from one's proper station — such a one may dwell in a royal household.

sanskrit: dakṣiṇaṃ vātha vāmaṃ vā pārśvam āsīta paṇḍitaḥ rakṣiṇāṃ hy āttaśastrāṇāṃ sthānaṃ paścād vidhīyate nityaṃ vipratiṣiddhaṃ tu purastād āsanaṃ mahat
english: A wise man should sit at the right or left side; the position behind is ordained for armed guards, and sitting directly in front is always strictly forbidden — it is a seat of great importance.

sanskrit: na ca saṃdarśane kiṃ cit pravṛddham api saṃjapet api hy etad daridrāṇāṃ vyalīkasthānam uttamam
english: One should not whisper anything at all during an audience, however important it may be; for even this is the foremost seat of offense for the poor.

sanskrit: na mṛṣābhihitaṃ rājño manuṣyeṣu prakāśayet yaṃ cāsūyanti rājānaḥ puruṣaṃ na vadec ca tam
english: One should not reveal among men what the king has spoken falsely, and one should not mention the person whom kings resent.

sanskrit: śūro 'smīti na dṛptaḥ syād buddhimān iti vā punaḥ priyam evācaran rājñaḥ priyo bhavati bhogavān
english: One should not be arrogant thinking 'I am a hero' or 'I am wise'; by doing only what is pleasing to the king, one becomes dear to him and enjoys his favor.

sanskrit: aiśvaryaṃ prāpya duṣprāpaṃ priyaṃ prāpya ca rājataḥ apramatto bhaved rājñaḥ priyeṣu ca hiteṣu ca
english: Having obtained power that was hard to obtain, and having won the king's favor, one should remain vigilant in what is dear and beneficial to the king.

sanskrit: yasya kopo mahābādhaḥ prasādaś ca mahāphalaḥ kas tasya manasāpīcched anarthaṃ prājñasaṃmataḥ
english: Whose anger is a great calamity and whose favor yields great fruit — who, deemed wise, would even in his mind desire ill toward such a one?

sanskrit: na coṣṭhau nirbhujej jātu na ca vākyaṃ samākṣipet sadā kṣutaṃ ca vātaṃ ca ṣṭhīvanaṃ cācarec chanaiḥ
english: One should never twist the lips, nor interrupt speech; one should always sneeze, pass wind, and spit quietly.

sanskrit: hāsyavastuṣu cāpy asya vartamāneṣu keṣu cit nātigāḍhaṃ prahṛṣyeta na cāpy unmattavad dhaset
english: Even when amusing things occur in his presence, one should not be excessively delighted, nor should one laugh like a madman.

sanskrit: na cātidhairyeṇa cared gurutāṃ hi vrajet tathā smitaṃ tu mṛdupūrveṇa darśayeta prasādajam
english: One should not comport oneself with excessive gravity, for that way one becomes heavy; rather, a gentle smile born of graciousness should be shown.

sanskrit: lābhe na harṣayed yas tu na vyathed yo 'vamānitaḥ asaṃmūḍhaś ca yo nityaṃ sa rājavasatiṃ vaset
english: One who does not rejoice at gain, who does not feel pain when dishonored, and who is always unconfused — such a one may dwell in a royal household.

sanskrit: rājānaṃ rājaputraṃ vā saṃvartayati yaḥ sadā amātyaḥ paṇḍito bhūtvā sa ciraṃ tiṣṭhati śriyam
english: A minister who, having become wise, always attends upon the king or a prince, long enjoys prosperity.

sanskrit: pragṛhītaś ca yo 'mātyo nigṛhītaś ca kāraṇaiḥ na nirbadhnāti rājānaṃ labhate pragrahaṃ punaḥ
english: A minister who is favored and also restrained with cause, and who does not bind the king with obligations, gains favor once more.

sanskrit: pratyakṣaṃ ca parokṣaṃ ca guṇavādī vicakṣaṇaḥ upajīvī bhaved rājño viṣaye cāpi yo vaset
english: A discerning dependant who speaks of virtues both in the king's presence and in his absence, and whoever dwells in the king's domain — such a one thrives.

sanskrit: amātyo hi balād bhoktuṃ rājānaṃ prārthayet tu yaḥ na sa tiṣṭhec ciraṃ sthānaṃ gacchec ca prāṇasaṃśayam
english: A minister who demands enjoyment from the king by force will not long keep his position and will come to danger of his life.

sanskrit: śreyaḥ sadātmano dṛṣṭvā paraṃ rājñā na saṃvadet viśeṣayen na rājānaṃ yogyābhūmiṣu sarvadā
english: Seeing always what is best for himself, one should not converse with the king about something superior, and one should never surpass the king in any domain where he is competent.

sanskrit: amlāno balavāñ śūraś chāyevānapagaḥ sadā satyavādī mṛdur dāntaḥ sa rājavasatiṃ vaset
english: One who is unfading, strong, brave, always present like a shadow, truthful, gentle, and self-controlled — such a one may dwell in a royal household.

sanskrit: anyasmin preṣyamāṇe tu purastād yaḥ samutpatet ahaṃ kiṃ karavāṇīti sa rājavasatiṃ vaset
english: One who, when another is being sent, steps forward first saying 'What shall I do?' — such a one may dwell in a royal household.

sanskrit: uṣṇe vā yadi vā śīte rātrau vā yadi vā divā ādiṣṭo na vikalpeta sa rājavasatiṃ vaset
english: One who, when commanded, does not make excuses whether in heat or cold, by night or by day — such a one may dwell in a royal household.

sanskrit: yo vai gṛhebhyaḥ pravasan priyāṇāṃ nānusaṃsmaret duḥkhena sukham anvicchet sa rājavasatiṃ vaset
english: One who, when away from home, does not dwell in memory of loved ones, and who seeks happiness even through hardship — such a one may dwell in a royal household.

sanskrit: samaveṣaṃ na kurvīta nātyuccaiḥ saṃnidhau haset mantraṃ na bahudhā kuryād evaṃ rājñaḥ priyo bhavet
english: One should not dress alike with the king, should not laugh too loudly in his presence, and should not make counsel widely known — thus one becomes dear to the king.

sanskrit: na karmaṇi niyuktaḥ san dhanaṃ kiṃ cid upaspṛśet prāpnoti hi haran dravyaṃ bandhanaṃ yadi vā vadham
english: One who is appointed to a task should not touch any wealth; for one who steals property gains either imprisonment or death.

sanskrit: yānaṃ vastram alaṃkāraṃ yac cānyat saṃprayacchati tad eva dhārayen nityam evaṃ priyataro bhavet
english: Whatever conveyance, garment, or ornament the king gives, along with anything else — one should always wear that alone; thus one becomes more beloved.

sanskrit: saṃvatsaram imaṃ tāta tathāśīlā bubhūṣavaḥ atha svaviṣayaṃ prāpya yathākāmaṃ cariṣyatha
english: Dear ones, for this one year, behave thus and desire to prosper; then, having reached your own domain, you will move about as you please.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca anuśiṣṭāḥ sma bhadraṃ te naitad vaktāsti kaś cana kuntīm ṛte mātaraṃ no viduraṃ ca mahāmatim
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: We have been instructed; good fortune to you. No one could say these things save our mother Kuntī and the great-minded Vidura.

sanskrit: yad evānantaraṃ kāryaṃ tad bhavān kartum arhati tāraṇāyāsya duḥkhasya prasthānāya jayāya ca
english: Whatever must now be done immediately, please do it — for our deliverance from this sorrow, for our departure, and for victory.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca evam uktas tato rājñā dhaumyo 'tha dvijasattamaḥ akarod vidhivat sarvaṃ prasthāne yad vidhīyate
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Thus addressed by the king, Dhaumya, the foremost of twice-born men, duly performed all that is prescribed for a departure.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ samidhya tān agnīn mantravac ca juhāva saḥ samṛddhivṛddhilābhāya pṛthivīvijayāya ca
english: He kindled their fires and made offerings with mantras for the increase of prosperity and abundance, and for the conquest of the earth.

sanskrit: agniṃ pradakṣiṇaṃ kṛtvā brāhmaṇāṃś ca tapodhanān yājñasenīṃ puraskṛtya ṣaḍ evātha pravavrajuḥ
english: Having circumambulated the fire and honored the brahmins who were rich in austerity, with Yājñasenī (Draupadī) at their head, the six of them then set out.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca te vīrā baddhanistriṃśās tatāyudhakalāpinaḥ baddhagodhāṅgulitrāṇāḥ kālindīm abhito yayuḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Those heroes, with their swords buckled on, their quivers of arrows strapped in place, and their leather finger-guards bound, went along the Kālindī river.

sanskrit: tatas te dakṣiṇaṃ tīram anvagacchan padātayaḥ vasanto giridurgeṣu vanadurgeṣu dhanvinaḥ
english: Then those archers proceeded on foot along the southern bank, dwelling in mountain fastnesses and forest strongholds.

sanskrit: vidhyanto mṛgajātāni maheṣvāsā mahābalāḥ uttareṇa daśārṇāṃs te pāñcālān dakṣiṇena tu
english: Those mighty archers, great bowmen, piercing various kinds of deer, passed with Dasharna to the north of them and Pāñcāla to the south.

sanskrit: antareṇa yakṛllomāñ śūrasenāṃś ca pāṇḍavāḥ lubdhā bruvāṇā matsyasya viṣayaṃ prāviśan vanāt
english: The Pāṇḍavas passed between Yakrilloma and Śūrasena, speaking as hunters, and entered the territory of Matsya from the forest.

sanskrit: tato janapadaṃ prāpya kṛṣṇā rājānam abravīt paśyaikapadyo dṛśyante kṣetrāṇi vividhāni ca
english: Then, having reached the inhabited country, Kṛṣṇa (Draupadī) said to the king: 'Look — plowed fields are visible on every side, and various kinds of fields can be seen.'

sanskrit: vyaktaṃ dūre virāṭasya rājadhānī bhaviṣyati vasāmeha parāṃ rātriṃ balavān me pariśramaḥ
english: 'Clearly the capital of Virāṭa must be far away. Let us spend the night here — my fatigue is great.'

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca dhanaṃjaya samudyamya pāñcālīṃ vaha bhārata rājadhānyāṃ nivatsyāmo vimuktāś ca vanāditaḥ
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: Dhanañjaya, O Bhārata, take up Pāñcālī and carry her; we shall dwell in the capital, freed at last from forest life.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tām ādāyārjunas tūrṇaṃ draupadīṃ gajarāḍ iva saṃprāpya nagarābhyāśam avatārayad arjunaḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Arjuna quickly took Draupadī and, like a lordly elephant, having reached the vicinity of the city, Arjuna set her down.

sanskrit: sa rājadhānīṃ saṃprāpya kaunteyo 'rjunam abravīt kvāyudhāni samāsajya pravekṣyāmaḥ puraṃ vayam
english: Having reached the capital, the son of Kuntī (Yudhiṣṭhira) said to Arjuna: 'Where shall we deposit our weapons and then enter the city?'

sanskrit: sāyudhāś ca vayaṃ tāta pravekṣyāmaḥ puraṃ yadi samudvegaṃ janasyāsya kariṣyāmo na saṃśayaḥ
english: 'If we enter the city armed, dear one, we will without doubt cause alarm among its people.'

sanskrit: tato dvādaśa varṣāṇi praveṣṭavyaṃ vanaṃ punaḥ ekasminn api vijñāte pratijñātaṃ hi nas tathā
english: 'Then we would have to enter the forest again for twelve years, for if even one of us is recognized, that is what we vowed.'

sanskrit: arjuna uvāca iyaṃ kūṭe manuṣyendra gahanā mahatī śamī bhīmaśākhā durārohā śmaśānasya samīpataḥ
english: Arjuna said: O lord of men, here on this eminence stands a great and dense shami tree with massive branches, hard to climb, near a cremation ground.

sanskrit: na cāpi vidyate kaś cin manuṣya iha pārthiva utpathe hi vane jātā mṛgavyālaniṣevite
english: 'And there is no one at all to be found here, O king, for it has grown in a pathless forest frequented by deer and serpents.'

sanskrit: samāsajyāyudhāny asyāṃ gacchāmo nagaraṃ prati evam atra yathājoṣaṃ vihariṣyāma bhārata
english: 'Let us hang our weapons on this tree and go toward the city; thus we shall move about here as we please, O Bhārata.'

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca evam uktvā sa rājānaṃ dharmātmānaṃ yudhiṣṭhiram pracakrame nidhānāya śastrāṇāṃ bharatarṣabha
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having spoken thus to the righteous-souled king Yudhiṣṭhira, he proceeded to deposit the weapons, O bull of the Bhāratas.

sanskrit: yena devān manuṣyāṃś ca sarpāṃś caikaratho 'jayat sphītāñjanapadāṃś cānyān ajayat kurunandanaḥ
english: With which bow the son of Kuru's joy, alone on his chariot, had conquered gods, men, and serpents, and had subdued other flourishing kingdoms —

sanskrit: tad udāraṃ mahāghoṣaṃ sapatnagaṇasūdanam apajyam akarot pārtho gāṇḍīvam abhayaṃkaram
english: — that noble, greatly resounding Gāṇḍīva, which strikes fear into enemies and destroys multitudes of foes, the son of Pṛthā (Arjuna) now unstrung.

sanskrit: yena vīraḥ kurukṣetram abhyarakṣat paraṃtapaḥ amuñcad dhanuṣas tasya jyām akṣayyāṃ yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
english: The bowstring of that bow with which the hero, scorcher of foes, had protected Kurukṣetra — its inexhaustible string — Yudhiṣṭhira unloosed.

sanskrit: pāñcālān yena saṃgrāme bhīmaseno 'jayat prabhuḥ pratyaṣedhad bahūn ekaḥ sapatnāṃś caiva digjaye
english: With which bow the mighty Bhīmasena had conquered the Pāñcālas in battle, and alone had repelled many enemies in the conquest of the directions —

sanskrit: niśamya yasya visphāraṃ vyadravanta raṇe pare parvatasyeva dīrṇasya visphoṭam aśaner iva
english: — hearing the twang of which, enemies fled in battle, like the crack of a splitting mountain or the burst of a thunderbolt —

sanskrit: saindhavaṃ yena rājānaṃ parāmṛṣata cānagha jyāpāśaṃ dhanuṣas tasya bhīmaseno 'vatārayat
english: — with which the blameless one had seized the king of Sindhu — the bowstring of that bow Bhīmasena now removed.

sanskrit: ajayat paścimām āśāṃ dhanuṣā yena pāṇḍavaḥ tasya maurvīm apākarṣac chūraḥ saṃkrandano yudhi
english: With which bow the Pāṇḍava had conquered the western quarter, the string of that bow the heroic Sankrandana (Arjuna) drew off in battle.

sanskrit: dakṣiṇāṃ dakṣiṇācāro diśaṃ yenājayat prabhuḥ apajyam akarod vīraḥ sahadevas tadāyudham
english: With which bow the lord, skilled in southern ways, had conquered the southern quarter — the hero Sahadeva now unstrung that weapon.

sanskrit: khaḍgāṃś ca pītān dīrghāṃś ca kalāpāṃś ca mahādhanān vipāṭhān kṣuradhārāṃś ca dhanurbhir nidadhuḥ saha
english: They deposited together with their bows their golden, long swords, their quivers of great worth, their scabbards, and their razor-edged arrows.

sanskrit: tām upāruhya nakulo dhanūṃṣi nidadhat svayam yāni tasyāvakāśāni dṛḍharūpāṇy amanyata
english: Nakula, climbing the tree, himself deposited the bows in those forks which he judged to be firm and solid.

sanskrit: yatra cāpaśyata sa vai tiro varṣāṇi varṣati tatra tāni dṛḍhaiḥ pāśaiḥ sugāḍhaṃ paryabandhata
english: And where he saw it had rained across the years he bound them there very tightly with strong cords.

sanskrit: śarīraṃ ca mṛtasyaikaṃ samabadhnanta pāṇḍavāḥ vivarjayiṣyanti narā dūrād eva śamīm imām ābaddhaṃ śavam atreti gandham āghrāya pūtikam
english: The Pāṇḍavas also bound there the body of one dead, so that men would stay away from this shami tree even from a distance, smelling the foul stench and thinking 'a corpse is tied here.'

sanskrit: aśītiśatavarṣeyaṃ mātā na iti vādinaḥ kuladharmo 'yam asmākaṃ pūrvair ācarito 'pi ca samāsajānā vṛkṣe 'sminn iti vai vyāharanti te
english: Those who said 'This is a mother aged a hundred and eighty years — it is not so' would declare: 'This is the family custom practiced by our ancestors too — hanging them upon this tree.'

sanskrit: ā gopālāvipālebhya ācakṣāṇāḥ paraṃtapāḥ ājagmur nagarābhyāśaṃ pārthāḥ śatrunibarhaṇāḥ
english: Telling their stories down to the cowherd boys and shepherd lads, the Pārthas, scorchers of foes, destroyers of enemies, came near to the city.

sanskrit: jayo jayanto vijayo jayatseno jayadbalaḥ iti guhyāni nāmāni cakre teṣāṃ yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
english: Jaya, Jayanta, Vijaya, Jayatsena, Jayadbala — these were the secret names that Yudhiṣṭhira assigned to them.

sanskrit: tato yathāpratijñābhiḥ prāviśan nagaraṃ mahat ajñātacaryāṃ vatsyanto rāṣṭre varṣaṃ trayodaśam
english: Then, true to their vows, they entered the great city, intending to live unrecognized in the kingdom through the thirteenth year.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tato virāṭaṃ prathamaṃ yudhiṣṭhiro; rājā sabhāyām upaviṣṭam āvrajat vaiḍūryarūpān pratimucya kāñcanān; akṣān sa kakṣe parigṛhya vāsasā
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then Yudhiṣṭhira approached Virāṭa first, the king seated in his assembly hall, having donned lapis-blue golden dice and holding them under his arm wrapped in cloth.

sanskrit: narādhipo rāṣṭrapatiṃ yaśasvinaṃ; mahāyaśāḥ kauravavaṃśavardhanaḥ mahānubhāvo nararājasatkṛto; durāsadas tīkṣṇaviṣo yathoragaḥ
english: The lord of men — of great renown, increaser of the Kaurava line, of great majesty, honored by the king of men, unapproachable as a sharp-venomed serpent — approached the glorious lord of the realm.

sanskrit: bālena rūpeṇa nararṣabho mahān; athārcirūpeṇa yathāmaras tathā mahābhrajālair iva saṃvṛto ravir; yathānalo bhasmavṛtaś ca vīryavān
english: That great bull among men appeared youthful in form, and radiant as an immortal; covered with brilliant rays like the sun, and mighty as fire concealed beneath ash.

sanskrit: tam āpatantaṃ prasamīkṣya pāṇḍavaṃ; virāṭarāḍ indum ivābhrasaṃvṛtam mantridvijān sūtamukhān viśas tathā; ye cāpi ke cit pariṣatsamāsate papraccha ko 'yaṃ prathamaṃ sameyivān; anena yo 'yaṃ prasamīkṣate sabhām
english: Seeing the Pāṇḍava approach like the moon covered by clouds, the king of Virāṭa asked his ministers, brahmins, and charioteers, as well as the commoners and all who were seated in the assembly: 'Who is this who has come first, and who is this one who now surveys the hall?'

sanskrit: na tu dvijo 'yaṃ bhavitā narottamaḥ; patiḥ pṛthivyā iti me manogatam na cāsya dāso na ratho na kuṇḍale; samīpato bhrājati cāyam indravat
english: 'He will not be a mere brahmin — he is the best of men; in my mind I think he must be a lord of the earth. He has no slave, no chariot, no earrings — yet he shines near us like Indra.'

sanskrit: śarīraliṅgair upasūcito hy ayaṃ; mūrdhābhiṣikto 'yam itīva mānasam samīpam āyāti ca me gatavyatho; yathā gajas tāmarasīṃ madotkaṭaḥ
english: 'His bodily marks point to this — in my mind it is as if he were a consecrated king. He approaches me free of distress, like a rutting elephant going to a lotus pond.'

sanskrit: vitarkayantaṃ tu nararṣabhas tadā; yudhiṣṭhiro 'bhyetya virāṭam abravīt samrāḍ vijānātv iha jīvitārthinaṃ; vinaṣṭasarvasvam upāgataṃ dvijam
english: While he was thus reflecting, that bull among men, Yudhiṣṭhira, approached Virāṭa and said: 'Let the emperor know that a brahmin who has lost all his wealth, seeking a livelihood, has come here.'

sanskrit: ihāham icchāmi tavānaghāntike; vastuṃ yathā kāmacaras tathā vibho tam abravīt svāgatam ity anantaraṃ; rājā prahṛṣṭaḥ pratisaṃgṛhāṇa ca
english: 'Here I wish to dwell near you, blameless one, moving freely as I please, O lord.' The king, filled with joy, immediately replied: 'Welcome! Accept my hospitality.'

sanskrit: kāmena tātābhivadāmy ahaṃ tvāṃ; kasyāsi rājño viṣayād ihāgataḥ gotraṃ ca nāmāpi ca śaṃsa tattvataḥ; kiṃ cāpi śilpaṃ tava vidyate kṛtam
english: 'I address you gladly, my friend — from whose king's territory have you come here? Tell me truly your clan and name, and what skill or craft you possess.'

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca yudhiṣṭhirasyāsam ahaṃ purā sakhā; vaiyāghrapadyaḥ punar asmi brāhmaṇaḥ akṣān pravaptuṃ kuśalo 'smi devitā; kaṅketi nāmnāsmi virāṭa viśrutaḥ
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: 'I was formerly a friend of Yudhiṣṭhira; I am a brahmin of the Vyaghrapada lineage. I am skilled at throwing dice and gambling. I am known, O Virāṭa, by the name Kanka.'

sanskrit: virāṭa uvāca dadāmi te hanta varaṃ yam icchasi; praśādhi matsyān vaśago hy ahaṃ tava priyā hi dhūrtā mama devinaḥ sadā; bhavāṃś ca devopama rājyam arhati
english: Virāṭa said: 'Come then, I grant you whatever boon you desire; command the Matsyas — I am at your disposal. My gamblers who are dear to me have always pleased me; and you, O equal of the gods, are worthy of a kingdom.'
